raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

Enable batch-invariant Qwen GatedDeltaNet execution for prefill, cached continuation
and decode under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. This replaces #49827 and addresses
the prefill-partitioning concerns in #48613. The submitter has completed
line-by-line review; maintainer feedback is requested. AI assistance was used.

## Why

Qwen GDN normally uses chunked arithmetic for prefill and recurrent arithmetic
for decode. These compute the same mathematical operation but do not necessarily
produce the same floating-point result. A request can therefore change its
output when the scheduler splits its prefill differently or mixes it with decode
requests. Enabling the backend support flag alone does not address that problem.

The goal is to make the GDN computation independent of those scheduling choices,
including continuation from cached state, within a fixed execution configuration.

## How

In BIC mode, all non-speculative Qwen GDN tokens use the existing recurrent
kernel. Prefill, continuation and decode retain the same convolution/recurrent
state and follow the same arithmetic rather than switching between chunked and
recurrent implementations.

The change also adds a Qwen-specific backend identity/support gate and disables
batch-dependent Inductor transformations in BIC mode. XPU and NIXL references
are updated for the backend identity. The non-BIC numerical route is unchanged;
there are no scheduler chunk-grid restrictions.

Speculative decoding is explicitly unsupported. Long prefills can be slower on
the recurrent route; this is a correctness change, not a performance improvement.

## Related Work

- #57280 fixes batch-dependent gated-normalization row tiling. This PR includes
  overlapping normalization policy needed by the tested GDN path. That overlap
  needs resolving before merge; it is not a separate normalization contribution.
- #45819 opens the GDN backend support gate. This PR additionally addresses
  numerical differences between prefill and decode.
- #55868 aligns prefill/cache chunk grids. This approach instead shares
  recurrent arithmetic across arbitrary token partitions.
- #49827 is the superseded predecessor, now closed.
- #60034 tracks BIC GEMM performance; #50299 tracks TP collective work.
  Neither is included here or establishes TP/EP determinism for this PR.

## Verification

Tested on H100, TP1, BF16, torch 2.14.0+cu130, with
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, on current head `8c9ff7e60a7f` based on upstream
main `8a8e2baa02cd`. All changed remote source/test checksums match this head.

The wheel is `0.32.0rc1.dev111+gbb1438a93`, four commits before the base.
CUDA/C++ sources, build inputs and CUDA dependencies are identical between
the wheel revision and source base. The intervening native change is to the
Rust frontend, which these Python/MRV1 checks do not use. The full regression,
serving, quality and performance matrix was rerun after the rebase; prior-base
results are not substituted here. Changed-file pre-commit also passed.

### Regression Tests

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| GDN kernels: existing non-BIC parity, exact mixed batches and partition/state reload | 11 passed |
| BIC compiler policy/cache key | 1 passed |
| Public Qwen online chunked-prefill regression | 1 passed |
| NIXL convolution-layout derivation | 11 passed |
| Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy and CI test tethering | Passed |

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

Activate the review venv so subprocesses use its `vllm` CLI, then run:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0
export VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py -v

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/compile/test_config.py -k bic_compiler -v

VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py -k qwen_gdn_chunked -v

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  -k test_derive_mamba_conv_split -v
```

</details>

### Serving

Each configuration ran eight public/synthetic text, image and conversation-history
cases five times, generating 32 tokens per request. Requests ran alone and in
heterogeneous loaded batches; mixed decode/prefill steps were observed.

External instrumentation hashed every full-vocabulary BF16 logit row before
sampling. Missing or duplicate records fail the check. Tokens, top-logprobs and
raw-logit hashes matched exactly across executions within each configuration.

| Model | Execution | Prefix cache | Requests / logit rows | Cached prompt tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | eager | off | 40 / 1,280 | 0 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | eager | on | 40 / 1,280 | 15,552 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | compiled | off | 40 / 1,280 | 0 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | compiled | on | 40 / 1,280 | 15,552 |
| Qwen3.5-4B | eager | off | 40 / 1,280 | 0 |

Cache off/on also agreed at all 256 case-positions within each execution mode.
**Eager and compiled did not agree bitwise:** all 256 positions differed between
those modes. These checks establish invariance in the tested configurations,
not equality between configurations. Cache hits establish prompt reuse, not
generated-token cross-turn state reuse.

### Performance And Quality

Unprofiled `vllm bench throughput`, Qwen3.5-0.8B, TP1/BF16/eager/cache-off:
three repetitions per mode in alternating order, four warmup prompts and sixteen
measured prompts. Each repetition processed 16,384 input and 2,048 output tokens.

| Mode | Elapsed seconds | Median requests/s | Median output tokens/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal | 11.219, 11.880, 11.144 | 1.4261 | 182.54 |
| BIC | 15.711, 13.845, 13.883 | 1.1525 | 147.52 |

BIC reached 80.81% of normal median throughput. This includes global BIC GEMM
and the GDN path; it does not isolate GDN overhead or measure serving TTFT.
Logit capture was disabled.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction</summary>

Repeat three times per mode, alternating order:

```bash
# Set BIC to 0 or 1; activate the matching review venv.
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=$BIC vllm bench throughput \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B --dtype bfloat16 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
  --num-prompts 16 --num-warmups 4 --seed 42 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager
```

All six fresh runs supplied the explicit random lengths above. Logs and JSON
confirm identical measured token counts across modes and repetitions.

</details>

GSM8K smoke: normal and BIC both scored 7/32, with no invalid responses.
This is not comprehensive quality validation or identical-response proof.
Output lengths differed, so those task timings are not performance evidence.

### CI And Remaining Limits

The rebased head is conflict-free according to GitHub. Fresh
[Intel CI build 14141](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/14141) has
failures including a Python-optimized subprocess timeout in
`test_is_kv_cache_spec_uniform` (498 passed in that job). This is not an
exactness assertion failure. The same focused test passed locally on the rebased
head with its original timeout; its XPU cause remains unresolved. The fresh docs
build passed. Previous-head failures below are retained as history:

The quantization job also fails the upstream ModelOpt NVFP4-to-FP8 test because
its `modelopt_fp4` source checkpoint is unsupported on XPU (76 passed in that
job). This test and the supported-format declaration are unchanged by this PR.
A proposed source-format test guard was checked in a scratch copy; it has not
been added to this GDN diff. The timeout needs an Intel child stack trace;
six local optimized-Python probes passed without increasing its 60-second limit.

- [Pre-commit gate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38474232819):
  failed contributor/label eligibility before running the code checks.
- [Docs build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35129014/):
  stopped because that pre-commit gate failed, before building the docs.
- [Intel CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/14082):
  failed jobs include registry/DNS and checkout failures before tests, plus one
  two-GPU Llama startup-error test timeout (18 passed, 4 skipped in that job).
  The timeout remains unresolved; local H100 validation does not replace XPU CI.

Local Sky job 8 wrote all completed-stage artifacts, but its outer status is
failed with exit 141. A lock-protected completed-stage resume exited 0 without
rerunning stages. The outer failure is not relabeled as success; validation
claims above come from audited XML, complete captures and equal-work logs.

MRV2, TP/EP, other hardware, multi-node and live disaggregated state transfer
are not validated here. Normalization overlap with #57280 remains a maintainer
design decision; we are not changing that policy further before review.
No universal determinism or merge readiness is claimed.

---

<details>
<summary>Pull Request Checklist</summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [ ] **Design Fit:** Maintainer decision on normalization overlap remains.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Rebased-head local checks complete; CI and coverage limits documented.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Local checks passed; submitter's line-by-line review complete.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Motivation, method, related work and evidence documented.

</details>
